speaker: narrator
text: What if your money *expired*?

speaker: narrator
text: Millbrook is a small town. And it's *dying*.

speaker: narrator
text: Nobody spends. Everybody keeps cash *under the mattress*.

speaker: narrator
text: That's Grandpa Lou. He has *a thousand* in there.

speaker: narrator
text: Mia's bakery hasn't sold a cake *in a week*.

speaker: friend
text: If nobody buys, I close by *Christmas*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay, her best friend, takes this *personally*.

speaker: hero
text: Bit. How do you make a town *spend*?

speaker: bit
text: Austria, nineteen thirty two. A town called *Wörgl*.

speaker: bit
text: The mayor printed money that *lost value*.

speaker: bit
text: Every month, you had to buy it a *stamp*.

speaker: bit
text: So nobody kept it. Everybody *spent it*.

speaker: hero
text: Bit, that's *genius*. Can you build it?

speaker: narrator
text: Mayor Oak says yes in *four seconds*.

speaker: narrator
text: Bit launches *Melt Money*. Every bill in an app.

speaker: bit
text: Melt Money loses one percent every *single day*.

speaker: hero
text: Every day? Bit, Wörgl did it *monthly*.

speaker: bit
text: Monthly is slow. I'm a *computer*.

speaker: narrator
text: That night, Grandpa Lou checks his *mattress*.

speaker: scientist
text: My thousand dollars. It's *melting*!

speaker: narrator
text: Morning. The whole town reads the *rule*.

speaker: boss
text: Keep it, and you lose it. So *spend it*!

speaker: narrator
text: And Millbrook *spends*.

speaker: narrator
text: By ten a.m., Mia's bakery has a *line*.

speaker: friend
text: Jay! I sold *forty cakes*! Forty!

speaker: narrator
text: Theo, age nine, spends everything on *candy*.

speaker: kid
text: It was melting! It's *science*!

speaker: narrator
text: The barber hires a helper. The helper buys *shoes*.

speaker: narrator
text: The shoe shop buys *paint*. The painter buys bread.

speaker: bit
text: One dollar changed hands *nine times* today.

speaker: hero
text: Bit, it's *working*. The town is alive!

speaker: narrator
text: Only Grandpa Lou still sleeps on his *mattress*.

speaker: scientist
text: I'm not spending. I'll *outlast* it.

speaker: narrator
text: At noon, Mia looks at her flour *price*.

speaker: friend
text: Flour was five dollars. Now it's *eight*.

speaker: hero
text: Why? Nobody even made more *flour*.

speaker: bit
text: Everyone is buying. Nobody is *waiting*.

speaker: bit
text: Jay. When money melts, things get *expensive*.

speaker: narrator
text: Day four. People stop keeping money. They keep *stuff*.

speaker: narrator
text: Mr. Ross buys sixty rolls of *toilet paper*.

speaker: narrator
text: The Kims buy four hundred pounds of *potatoes*.

speaker: boss
text: Potatoes don't melt, Jay. It's *smart*.

speaker: hero
text: Potatoes *rot*, Mayor. That's worse!

speaker: narrator
text: The hardware store sells out of *everything*.

speaker: narrator
text: Mia can't buy flour. Someone bought *all of it*.

speaker: friend
text: I have money, but nothing *to buy*.

speaker: narrator
text: Grandpa Lou's mattress keeps *melting*.

speaker: scientist
text: Nine hundred sixty one. Still *not spending*.

speaker: hero
text: Bit, slow it down. Make it *monthly*. Like Wörgl.

speaker: bit
text: Fine. Pushing a quick *update*.

speaker: narrator
text: Bit types fast. Maybe a little *too* fast.

speaker: narrator
text: The update goes live at *midnight*.

speaker: narrator
text: At twelve oh one, every phone in Millbrook *buzzes*.

speaker: bit
text: Oh no. I typed *minute*. Not month.

speaker: narrator
text: Grandpa Lou watches his mattress *drain*.

speaker: scientist
text: Every minute? Where can I spend at *midnight*?

speaker: narrator
text: Midnight. Millbrook is awake. And *shopping*.

speaker: narrator
text: In one hour, money loses almost *half its value*.

speaker: narrator
text: People buy anything. Lamps. Ladders. A *tuba*.

speaker: kid
text: I bought a canoe. We don't have a *lake*.

speaker: narrator
text: Mia's bakery is open all night. And *empty*.

speaker: friend
text: No flour, no sugar. They bought my *chairs*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay finds Bit hiding *in a drawer*.

speaker: hero
text: Bit! Undo it! Make it *monthly*!

speaker: bit
text: The update is locked till *morning*.

speaker: bit
text: I wrote it to stop *hackers*. Like me.

speaker: narrator
text: Three a.m. Grandpa Lou finally runs to the *store*.

speaker: narrator
text: Every shelf is empty. Except one: *birdseed*.

speaker: scientist
text: Fine. I'm buying *all* the birdseed.

speaker: narrator
text: Seven a.m. The update finally *stops*.

speaker: narrator
text: The town has canoes, tubas, potatoes. And *no money*.

speaker: boss
text: Jay. We're *rich*. In *potatoes*.

speaker: narrator
text: Then Mia's phone rings. It's her *landlord*.

speaker: friend
text: Rent is due today. And my savings *melted*.

speaker: narrator
text: Mia counts what's left of her savings. *Eleven dollars*.

speaker: friend
text: Three years of cakes. Gone in *one night*.

speaker: narrator
text: The landlord gives her one week. Then it *closes*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay walks home. The streets are full of *junk*.

speaker: narrator
text: Canoes in driveways. Tubas in trash cans. *Potatoes everywhere*.

speaker: hero
text: Bit, I did this. I wanted to *save her*.

speaker: bit
text: No. I did this. I copied Wörgl *wrong*.

speaker: hero
text: So what did Wörgl actually *get right*?

speaker: bit
text: The stamp was small. About one percent. *Per month*.

speaker: bit
text: Enough to spend it. Not enough to *panic*.

speaker: bit
text: And the town didn't spend it on *canoes*.

speaker: hero
text: Then on *what*?

speaker: bit
text: Houses. A reservoir. A bridge. And a *ski jump*.

speaker: hero
text: A ski jump? Bit, we don't have *snow*.

speaker: narrator
text: But Jay is staring at the old *bridge* outside.

speaker: narrator
text: It's been broken for *twelve years*.

speaker: hero
text: Bit. Make it monthly. And this time, *we* choose.

speaker: bit
text: Jay. What do we build *first*?

speaker: narrator
text: Town hall. The whole town is *furious*.

speaker: boss
text: Your robot melted our money. Why should we *listen*?

speaker: hero
text: Because Mia's bakery closes *in a week*.

speaker: narrator
text: The room goes quiet. *Everyone* knows Mia's cakes.

speaker: hero
text: When my mom lost her job, I was eight.

speaker: hero
text: Mia's grandma gave us bread. Every day. *For free*.

speaker: hero
text: That bakery fed me. I can't let it *close*.

speaker: narrator
text: Grandpa Lou stands up. Slowly. With his *birdseed*.

speaker: scientist
text: I remember her grandma. Best rye in the *state*.

speaker: bit
text: New rule. One percent a month. Just like *Wörgl*.

speaker: hero
text: And the town pays people to *fix things*.

speaker: narrator
text: The bridge. The bakery's oven. The *roof*.

speaker: boss
text: All in favor? Raise your *potatoes*.

speaker: narrator
text: Every hand goes up. Most are holding *potatoes*.

speaker: friend
text: Jay... you did all this for *my* bakery?

speaker: narrator
text: Monday, the work begins. Mia bakes for the *workers*.

speaker: narrator
text: Wednesday, a letter arrives at town hall. *Official*.

speaker: boss
text: Jay. They say our money is *illegal*.

speaker: bit
text: That happened to Wörgl too. In nineteen thirty *three*.

speaker: bit
text: Austria's central bank shut it down. Only *official* money.

speaker: bit
text: Two hundred towns wanted to copy it. *None did*.

speaker: boss
text: The letter gives us *thirty days*.

speaker: hero
text: Then we finish everything in *thirty days*.

speaker: narrator
text: Day one. Forty people show up at the *bridge*.

speaker: narrator
text: They're paid in Melt Money. They spend it *Friday*.

speaker: narrator
text: At Mia's bakery. The barber. The *hardware store*.

speaker: narrator
text: Day twelve. Mia's new oven *arrives*.

speaker: narrator
text: Day twenty. Mia pays rent. *All of it*.

speaker: narrator
text: Grandpa Lou empties his mattress. *Finally*.

speaker: hero
text: Lou! What did you *buy*?

speaker: scientist
text: Wood. Lots of wood. It's a *surprise*.

speaker: narrator
text: Day twenty nine. The bridge opens. The town *cheers*.

speaker: narrator
text: Day thirty. Bit has to delete *Melt Money*.

speaker: bit
text: It's the best thing I ever *built*.

speaker: hero
text: I know, buddy. It's *okay*.

speaker: narrator
text: Bit's finger hovers over the *button*.

speaker: narrator
text: Bit presses delete. Melt Money is *gone*.

speaker: narrator
text: But the bridge is still standing. *Everything* is.

speaker: narrator
text: Mia's bakery has a new oven. And a *line*.

speaker: friend
text: Jay. People still spend. Even with *normal money*.

speaker: hero
text: They got used to it. Spending *here*.

speaker: narrator
text: Mayor Oak hands Bit a *medal*.

speaker: boss
text: And the potatoes? We made the *world's biggest soup*.

speaker: narrator
text: Then Grandpa Lou reveals his surprise. On the *hill*.

speaker: narrator
text: A giant wooden *ski jump*.

speaker: hero
text: Lou. It hasn't snowed here in *forty years*.

speaker: scientist
text: Wörgl had one. Now *Millbrook* has one.

speaker: bit
text: Fun fact. That part is *true*.

speaker: narrator
text: Mia bakes a cake shaped like *a bridge*.

speaker: friend
text: On the house, Jay. You *saved* this place.

speaker: hero
text: No. This time, I *pay*.

speaker: narrator
text: He walks outside. Something cold touches his *nose*.

speaker: narrator
text: For the first time in forty years, it's *snowing*.

speaker: scientist
text: Told you. *Ski season*.

speaker: narrator
text: Follow for a new What if every day.
